examples.text: Na die verkeerde zet zag de beroemde schaakspeler zich gedwongen op te geven.

examples.text: Hij gaf hoog op over die toespraak van Obama.

glosses: ergens mee stoppen/niet mee doorgaan, niet voortzetten

examples.text: Toch was hij ook eigen plannen gaan ontwikkelen. Hij wilde weg, hij voelde wel wat voor Tonkin, al wist hij zelf niet goed waarom. In ieder geval wilde hij het beroep van boekhouder opgeven en iets anders gaan doen.
Nooit stoppen en opgeven op een slechte dag, had ik gehoord.

glosses: als verloren beschouwen

examples.text: De strijders zullen bepaalde gebieden in de toekomst toch moeten opgeven.

glosses: aanreiken

translations.source_sense_description: de strijd staken en zich gewonnen geven

glosses: etwas Sinnloses beenden, aufhören, einstellen; etwas beenden, obwohl der Sinn im Weitermachen besteht

examples.text: Der Läufer gab nach einem Sturz auf.
Verneinung: Obwohl sie seit drei Jahren verschwunden ist, haben Meiers ihre kleine Tochter noch nicht aufgegeben.
„[…] die Brexit-Gegner werden nicht einfach aufgeben, nur weil es jetzt einen neuen Premierminister [B. Johnson] gibt.“
Die Mannschaft gab das sinkende Schiff auf.
Wegen mangelnder Aufträge musste ich meinen Betrieb aufgeben, nachdem die Bank meine Kreditlinie nicht weiter erhöhen wollte.
Diese Mühle wurde schon vor Jahren aufgegeben.
„Sie war eine der wenigen, die noch nicht aufgegeben hatten. Sie würde nie aufgeben.“

glosses: jemandem (etwas) aufgeben: etwas zur Erledigung auftragen, zur Aufgabe machen

examples.text: Ich hatte Ihnen doch aufgegeben, den Rasen zu mähen!
Ab Morgen sind Ferien, deswegen gebe ich euch keine Hausaufgaben auf.
Die Mathelehrerin gibt den Kindern viel zu viel auf.
Ihr Verschwinden gab uns viele Rätsel auf.

glosses: jemandem etwas zur Beförderung oder Bearbeitung übergeben

examples.text: Ich werde zur Zeitung gehen und ein Inserat aufgeben.
Bitte geben Sie diesen Brief noch bei der Post auf.
Nachdem wir unsere Bestellungen aufgegeben hatten, konnten wir uns in Ruhe unterhalten.

glosses: keine Hoffnung mehr auf Genesung/Rettung von jemandem haben, jemanden als tot/verloren betrachten

examples.text: „Am Aschermittwoch erhielt ich in der Frühe einen Brief von C. C., daß der Arzt ihre Freundin aufgegeben hätte; diese könne höchstens noch etwa vierzehn Tage leben. “

translations.source_sense_description: de strijd staken en zich gewonnen geven

glosses: To surrender (someone or something); to inform on (someone).

examples.text: He was surrounded, so gave himself up.
They gave him up to the police.

glosses: To relinquish (something)

examples.text: He gave up his seat to an old man.
The king gave up land in exchange for peace.
"Dear Miss Woodhouse, I would not give up the pleasure and honour of being intimate with you for any thing in the world."

glosses: To have someone obtain (something) to one's disadvantage; to concede.

examples.text: A good pitcher will give up very few home runs.
Don't tell them where you are, and try not to give up any clues either.

Fiers, who now pitches for the Oakland Athletics, has gone 27-12 with a no-hitter in two years since leaving the Astros. But the last time he faced them, on Sept. 9, he gave up nine runs, including five homers, and got just three outs.

glosses: To stop or quit (an activity, etc.)

examples.text: They gave up the search when it got dark.

Once again, the WiFi isn't willing to work. When the guard comes to check tickets, I ask him if it ever works. He rolls his eyes and tells me it rarely does. He says I'll be lucky if I get it to connect. I give up trying.

glosses: To abandon (someone or something)

examples.text: I gave up my faith years ago.
The semi-streamlined contour of the earlier G.W.R. railcars has been given up in favour of a more utilitarian blunt-nose end, and effective floor space gained thereby.
Never gonna give you up / Never gonna let you down / Never gonna run around and desert you

The optimistic peace-and-love philosophy of his youth having given him up, he no longer knew how to reconcile himself to an increasingly phoney (he loathed, in this context, the otherwise excellent word “virtual”) reality.
"I tried retirement ten years ago. Didn't think much of it. Complete waste of time. So I gave it up after two weeks."

glosses: To lose hope concerning (someone or something)

examples.text: They gave him up for dead.

glosses: To admit defeat, capitulate.

examples.text: OK, I give up, you win.

Wake in a sweat again / Another day's been laid to waste / In my disgrace / Stuck in my head again / Feels like I'll never leave this place / There's no escape / I'm my own worst enemy / I've given up / I'm sick of feeling / Is there nothing you can say? / Take this all away / I'm suffocating

glosses: To execute a trade on behalf of another broker.
To acknowledge, recognize as.

examples.text: The next morning, Sunday, I was boxing with R., who had come over with three or four others to swap a few with me. I was given up to be the best boxer around, and I laid them cold as fast as they came at me.

glosses: To reveal (something).

examples.text: He gave up that he was the one who opened the door.
Well, give it up, Prof! What did you find out!

glosses: Become fully taken over by a certain quality, activity, trait, etc.

examples.text: And now She Seems give up to Sin / Too much neglecting grace within

translations.source_sense_description: de strijd staken en zich gewonnen geven

glosses: Retroceder, marchar hacia atrás.
Retroceder las bestias que tiran de un carruaje.
Aflojar o ceder en un negocio, empeño o discusión.

examples.text: He recurrido a todo pero no he conseguido nada. Pero ni aún así cejaré en mi empeño.

glosses: To relate details of (an event or incident); to recount, describe (something).

examples.text: Many of these classic methods are still used, with some modern improvements. For example, with the aid of special microphones and automated sound detection software, ornithologists recently reported[…]that pine siskins (Spinus pinus) undergo an irregular, nomadic type of nocturnal migration.

glosses: To repeat (something one has heard), to retell; to pass on, convey (a message, information etc.).
To take oneself (to someone or something) for guidance or support; to appeal.

examples.text: thenne they ansuerd by and by that they coude not excuse the quene /[…]/ Allas sayd the quene I made this dyner for a good entente / and neuer for none euyl soo almyghty god me help in my ryght as I was neuer purposed to doo suche euylle dedes / and that I reporte me vnto god

glosses: To notify someone of (particular intelligence, suspicions, illegality, misconduct etc.); to make notification to relevant authorities; to submit a formal report of.

examples.text: For insurance reasons, I had to report the theft to the local police station.

glosses: To make a formal statement, especially of complaint, about (someone).

examples.text: If you do that again I'll report you to the boss.

glosses: To show up or appear at an appointed time; to present oneself.
To write news reports (for); to cover as a journalist or reporter.

examples.text: Andrew Marr reports now on more in-fighting at Westminster.
Every newspaper reported the war.
In January, the country’s weather agency sent aircraft to release chemicals into clouds over the Yellow Sea, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency reported.

glosses: To be accountable to or subordinate to (someone) in a hierarchy; to receive orders from (someone); to give official updates to (someone who is above oneself in a hierarchy).

examples.text: The financial director reports to the CEO.
Now that I've been promoted, I report to Benjamin, whom I loathe.

glosses: To return or present as the result of an examination or consideration of any matter officially referred.

examples.text: The committee reported the bill with amendments, or reported a new bill, or reported the results of an inquiry.

glosses: To take minutes of (a speech, the doings of a public body, etc.); to write down from the lips of a speaker.
To refer.

examples.text: Baldwine his ſonne, the fourth of that name [Baldwin IV of Jerusalem], ſucceeded his father [Amalric of Jerusalem]: ſo like unto him, that we report the reader to the character of King Almerick, and will ſpare the repeating his description.

glosses: To return or repeat, as sound; to echo.

examples.text: a church with windows only from above[…] that reporteth the voice twelve or thirteen times

glosses: Of a ship, to return to a port.

examples.text: Our ship leaves port on Monday and will re-port on Friday.

glosses: A piece of information describing, or an account of certain events given or presented to someone, with the most common adpositions being by (referring to creator of the report) and on (referring to the subject).

examples.text: A report by the telecommunications ministry on the phone network revealed a severe capacity problem.
Hospitals are failing to care properly for the growing number of people with dementia, according to an NHS-funded report, which has prompted demands for big improvements to help patients.

glosses: Reputation.

examples.text: I love thee in such sort / As, thou being mine, mine is thy good report.
Certain it is that if he had been daft before, he now ran wild in his pranks, and an evil report of him was in every mouth.

glosses: The sharp, loud sound from a gun or explosion.

examples.text: While their masters, the mates, seemed afraid of the sound of the hinges of their own jaws, the harpooneers chewed their food with such a relish that there was a report to it.
[…] a pistol-shot, flash and report, came from the hedge-side.

He knelt upon one knee, cocked the weapon, placed the muzzle against the man's forehead, and turning away his eyes pulled the trigger. There was no report. He had used his last cartridge for the horse.

Waziri’s warriors marched at a rapid trot through the jungle in the direction of the village. For a few minutes, the sharp cracking of guns ahead warned them to haste, but finally the reports dwindled to an occasional shot, presently ceasing altogether.

glosses: An employee whose position in a corporate hierarchy is below that of a particular manager.

examples.text: The revelation that boss of one year Laurent Freixe was conducting an undisclosed affair with a direct report has rocked a 159-year-old conglomerate that pioneered infant formula and milk chocolate before growing to become the world's largest food and beverage company.
